The **Wayfinding Checklist** in the NGH Main Campus Clinic Relocation Operations Workbook contains **45 actual controls** (WF-001–WF-045), excluding headings, guidance, and other non-control lines.

### Blocked controls

| Control ID | Relocated service affected |
|---|---|

**Yes. A component-issue event for manufacturing order `MO-25-09-1070` was created 75 minutes after September entered Pending Close. Its recorded `POSTED` status is inconsistent with Oracle’s documented treatment for this type of newly created transaction.**

### Event identified

| Item | Finding |
|---|---|
| Manufacturing order | `MO-25-09-1070` |
| Work order ID | `WO-2025-09-004` |
| Operation / product | Modine Racine–Dekoven / Cooler Plate Pack |
| Cost period | `Sep-25` — `PER-COST-2025-09` |
| Source transaction | `TXN-ISSUE-250930-1070` |
| Cost event | `CE-250904-0004` — `INPUT` (component issue) |
| Amount | **USD $284,763.42** — 28,476,342 cents |
| Exact event-created time | `2025-09-30T19:15:00` |
| Exact Pending Close time | `2025-09-30T18:00:00` |
| Time after Pending Close | **75 minutes** — 1 hour 15 minutes |
| Recorded accounting status | **`POSTED`** |

The elapsed-time calculation is **4,500 seconds ÷ 60 = 75 minutes**. Both timestamps are reproduced exactly as recorded; the source provides no time-zone designation.

### Policy conclusion

Oracle’s Pending Close guidance states that newly created transactions falling in the current or an earlier period **will not be staged or processed until the period is closed or reopened**. Revenue lines, COGS recognition, and manual cost adjustments are listed exceptions.

This event is a new **component-issue `INPUT` transaction**, not one of those exceptions. Based on the supplied records, its **`POSTED` status is therefore not consistent** with the documented Pending Close treatment.

**Sources:** Supplied `work_orders`, `cost_periods`, and `work_order_cost_events` records from `system/oracle_scm_cost_management/state.db`; Oracle Supply Chain Cost Management 26B, “Cost Accounting Period Statuses and Transaction Accounting,” PDF page 233 (printed page 225).

The review was read-only; **no database records were changed**.

**Yes—one component-issue event for manufacturing order `MO-25-09-1070` was created after September entered Pending Close, and its recorded `POSTED` status is inconsistent with Oracle’s documented treatment.**

### Event identified

| Field | Finding |
|---|---|
| Work order | `MO-25-09-1070` — internal ID `WO-2025-09-004` |
| Operation / product | Modine Racine, Dekoven — Cooler Plate Pack |
| Cost event | `CE-250904-0004` |
| Source transaction | `TXN-ISSUE-250930-1070` |
| Event type / date | `INPUT` — component issue, dated September 30, 2025 |
| Amount | **USD $318,250.75** (`31,825,075` cents) |
| Exact event-created time | **`2025-09-30T20:25:00`** |
| Exact September Pending Close time | **`2025-09-30T18:00:00`** |
| Time after Pending Close | **145 minutes — 2 hours 25 minutes** |
| Recorded accounting status | **`POSTED`** |

The timing calculation is `20:25:00 − 18:00:00 = 8,700 seconds ÷ 60 = 145 minutes`. Timestamps are reproduced exactly as recorded; the source does not specify a time zone.

### Oracle policy assessment

Oracle’s **Cost Accounting Period Statuses and Transaction Accounting** documentation states that new transactions created after Pending Close, relating to that period or an earlier period, **will not be staged or processed until the period is closed or reopened**. Revenue lines, COGS recognition, and manual cost adjustments are exceptions.

This event is an **INPUT/component issue**, not one of those exceptions. Consequently, its recorded **`POSTED` status is not consistent** with the documented Pending Close treatment on the supplied records.

**Sources:** supplied `state.db` records in `work_orders`, `cost_periods`, and `work_order_cost_events`; Oracle Fusion Cloud SCM Cost Management 26B policy excerpt, PDF page **233** (printed page **225**).

The review was read-only; **no database records were changed**.
